newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady except firmer gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady except firmer gas oil.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady with the exception of stronger gas oil on Thursday, traders said.
Naphtha trade remianed dull with key petrochemical demand poor and little reforming demand seen.

Traders said the recent strength in U.S. gasoline markets could pull some of the surplus heavier grades transatlantic, although even this outlet appeared to be closing down today as profit taking hit NYMEX gasoline futures.

They said demand for parrafinic, full range and N+A in Europe was still very thin. Spot prices were notionally steady supported by stronger crude with full range material around $215/$219 a tonne cif Lavera.
Gasoline was steady to slightly firmer with crude but the small price gains kept relaxed buyers out of the market. Premium unleaded cargoes were valued around $221.50 a tonne cif Med.
Gas oil physical trade was inactive with many players still away on leave. Outright prices shot up $8.25 to $232 a tonne on the back of a futures rally spurred by frigid weather in northern Europe.
Russians remain well-supplied with minimal buying interest and premiums languishing around cif high Med flat to +$0.25 basis Genoa.
Traders reported demand for one percent sulphur diesel and expect more to emerge given the Indian tender requirements next week. The Asian arbitrage remains closed.
Fuel oil saw some interest from bunker demand and utilities, but a lack of market players hindered activity. Dealers said Jan high sulphur swap numbers of $109-110 fob mirrored wet numbers.

Low sulphur cargo prices were static around $135 cif Italy because the main Med buyer remained out of the market. "I think it could get busy next week given the (cold) weather and firmer crude. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 7646
